screening.reason: Reports a diagnostic-prediction (ASD vs TD classification) analysis of ABIDE I resting-state fMRI (CC200/CC400 C-PAC-derived correlation matrices plus topological features); satisfies inclusion 2-3.

evidence_spans.text: ABIDE dataset [4,7] consists of resting state fMRI brain scans from 16 diﬀerent imaging sites.
evidence_spans.claim: Cohort was ABIDE I, 16 imaging sites.

evidence_spans.text:
We use Craddock 200 (CC200) data set, where the
imaging data is ﬁrst preprocessed using the Conﬁgurable Pipeline for Analysis
of Connectomes (CPAC) and then the mean blood oxygenation level dependent
(BOLD) signals for 200 regions of interest (ROIs) are extracted. After ﬁltering
for missing and invalid data, it contains 1035 subjects, of which 505 are ASD
patients and 530 are TDC (typically developing control subjects).
evidence_spans.claim: Used the CC200 (and CC400) C-PAC-derived parcellation; after filtering, N=1035 (505 ASD/530 TDC).

evidence_spans.text:
The present state-of-the-art machine learning model using deep learning has a
classiﬁcation accuracy of 70.2% on the ABIDE (Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange) data
set.
evidence_spans.claim: Cites prior state-of-the-art deep-learning accuracy of 70.2% on ABIDE (Heinsfeld et al.) as benchmark.

evidence_spans.text:
With this approach, even with a simple 3-layer neural network, we are able to achieve a
classiﬁcation accuracy of 69.2% on the
ABIDE data set.
evidence_spans.claim: The hybrid topological+correlation 3-layer neural network achieved 69.2% classification accuracy.

evidence_spans.text:
However, our experiments also show that the improvement due to topological features is not always statisti-
cally signiﬁcant. Therefore, we oﬀer a cautionary tale to the practitioners
regarding the limited discriminative power of topological features derived from
fMRI data for the classiﬁcation of autism.
evidence_spans.claim: Main finding: topological-feature improvements over correlation-only features are not always statistically significant.

evidence_spans.text:
All results are
obtained by running a 5-fold stratiﬁed cross-validation scheme where we report the mean classiﬁca-
tion accuracy over all folds.

we esti-
mate the p-values using a Monte-Carlo approximation with 100, 000 samples.
evidence_spans.claim: Statistical significance of accuracy improvements assessed via a Monte-Carlo permutation test (100,000 samples).

assessments.support: Full ABIDE I (16 sites), N and diagnosis breakdown (505 ASD/530 TDC) given after filtering for missing/invalid data.
CC200/CC400 C-PAC-derived parcellations named; correlation matrices plus topological (persistence diagram/image/landscape) features clearly described.
Diagnostic labels taken from ABIDE as distributed; diagnostic instrument not restated in this paper.

5-fold stratified cross-validation with a Monte-Carlo permutation test for statistical significance of model comparisons; the paper explicitly reports that topological-feature gains are often not significant, avoiding overstated single-split claims; however no leave-site-out evaluation or explicit site handling is reported for the pooled 16-site CV.

risk_of_bias.summary: A methodologically careful, self-critical predictive-modelling paper (explicitly testing and reporting non-significance of claimed improvements) using stratified cross-validation and permutation testing, though without leave-site-out evaluation across the pooled 16-site ABIDE sample.

charting.title: Autism Classification Using Topological Features and Deep Learning: A Cautionary Tale
charting.journal_conference: MICCAI (Medical Image Computing and Computer Assisted Intervention)
charting.dataset_openly_available: Uses the publicly available Preprocessed Connectomes Project ABIDE CC200/CC400 derivatives; no study-specific code/participant-list repository link found in the text
charting.specific_features: ROI-pairwise Pearson correlation matrices (CC200/CC400) combined with persistence diagrams/images/landscapes (topological data analysis) of the correlation-derived point cloud
charting.feature_extraction_tools: C-PAC pipeline (CC200 and CC400 Craddock parcellations, Preprocessed Connectomes Project); sklearn-tda for topological features
charting.model_category: SVM, Random Forest, Neural Network (including a hybrid correlation+topological NN)
charting.specific_algorithms: Linear SVM, Random Forest (500 trees, depth 5), fully-connected NN, hybrid NN combining correlation and persistence-diagram features
charting.validation_methodology: 5-fold stratified cross-validation; Monte-Carlo permutation testing (100,000 samples) for statistical comparison between models
charting.key_performance_results: Hybrid topological+correlation 3-layer NN: 69.2% accuracy (vs cited prior state-of-the-art of 70.2% using deep learning alone on ABIDE); improvement from adding topological features was not always statistically significant
charting.summary_key_findings: On ABIDE I CC200/CC400 data (N=1035; 505 ASD/530 TDC), combining topological (persistence-diagram/landscape) features with functional-connectivity correlation features in SVM/RF/NN classifiers achieved up to 69.2% accuracy with a simple 3-layer neural network, but permutation testing showed the improvement from adding topological features over correlation features alone was not always statistically significant, offering a cautionary methodological conclusion for TDA-based autism classification.
charting.reviewer_notes: A methods-cautionary paper explicitly testing (and often rejecting) the claimed benefit of topological features for ASD classification.

narrative_row.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction; ABIDE I, 16 sites (CC200/CC400 C-PAC derivatives); n=505 ASD / 530 TDC (N=1035).
narrative_row.methods: C-PAC-derived CC200/CC400 correlation matrices combined with topological features (persistence diagrams/images/landscapes); SVM, Random Forest, and hybrid NN classifiers; 5-fold stratified cross-validation with Monte-Carlo permutation significance testing.
narrative_row.outcomes: Best accuracy 69.2% using a hybrid topological+correlation 3-layer NN; improvement from topological features over correlation alone was not always statistically significant.
narrative_row.key_limitations: No leave-site-out evaluation despite 16 pooled sites; no quantitative motion/QC threshold reported in this paper; no study-specific code/data release; authors themselves caution against overinterpreting topological-feature gains.
narrative_row.relevance_notes: A self-critical benchmark of topological-data-analysis features for ABIDE ASD classification, useful as a cautionary methodological reference in the knowledge graph.
